text: Trungnam secures key equipment deals for $2.2 billion Cà Ná LNG power project

HÀ NỘI - A consortium led by Trungnam Group has signed an equipment supply contract with Italy's Ansaldo Energia and a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with China's Shanghai Electric to advance the development of the nearly US$2.2 billion Cà Ná liquefied natural gas (LNG) power project in Khánh Hòa Province.
The agreements mark a step forward in securing key equipment packages for the 1,500-MWpower plant, which is targeted to begin commercial operations in 2030, Trungnam said.
Under the contract, Ansaldo Energia will supply two GT36 gas turbine units, generators and associated auxiliary systems.
The GT36 is an H-class gas turbine featuring sequential combustion technology with two combustion chambers arranged in series.
The design enables high efficiency at both full and partial loads, improves operational flexibility and helps control nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions.

These capabilities are particularly relevant as Việt Nam's power system incorporates a growing share of renewable energy, requiring conventional power plants to provide flexible and reliable backup capacity.
Once operational, the Cà Ná LNG plant is expected to supply approximately 9 billion kWh of electricity annually to the national grid to help meet rising power demand and strengthen energy security.

Trungnam Chairman Nguyễn Tâm Thịnh said the cooperation with Ansaldo Energia will extend beyond equipment supply to include project development, technology selection, technical support and operational services.

The two companies will also explore solutions to support Việt Nam's energy transition, including improving gas-fired power plant efficiency, optimising operations and gradually adopting cleaner fuels, he said.
Separately, Trungnam and Shanghai Electric signed an MoU establishing a framework for cooperation on equipment for the plant's steam power generation cycle.

Under the proposed arrangement, Shanghai Electric is expected to supply steam turbine units, steam turbine generators, heat recovery steam generators (HRSGs), condensers and related auxiliary systems.
These components form an essential part of a combined-cycle power plant, which captures heat from gas turbine exhaust to generate additional electricity and improve overall plant efficiency.
The company said it was focusing resources on equipment procurement and project preparation to keep the Ca Na LNG power plant on track for completion and operation in 2030. - VNS
